sec-head.h2: RAG vs long context evaluation services
sec-head.p: Architecture assessments and builds tailored to your cost, accuracy, and freshness requirements.

card.p: An independent evaluation of your use case—data volume, latency budget, update frequency—resulting in a written recommendation: RAG, long context, or a hybrid, with cost and accuracy trade-offs quantified.
Retrieval-first builds with chunking, embedding, and re-ranking optimized for freshness and low cost. Ideal for dynamic knowledge bases where documents update frequently.
Systems designed to leverage million-token models (Gemini 1.5, Claude 3) with prompt compression, sliding windows, and context caching to maximize accuracy per token dollar.
A tiered approach: RAG for large, dynamic corpora and long context for single-document deep dives or conversation history, routing queries by scope and freshness needs.
Assessment for teams currently locked into one approach, identifying where switching or augmenting could reduce latency, improve answer quality, or cut inference costs by 30–50%.

card cta-card.p: Try the fit-check widget above, or get it scoped properly.

card.h3: Cost, freshness, or scale is the priority
ul: Your knowledge base exceeds 100k tokens and updates daily: RAG costs ~$0.002 per query vs $0.10+ for long context at 1M tokens
Freshness is critical—RAG retrieves the latest indexed content instantly; long context requires re-embedding or re-prompting with new data
Accuracy on narrow, factoid questions: retrieval precision (top-5 recall >95%) beats long context's tendency to hallucinate on peripheral details
You need to serve many users with low latency—RAG's sub-second retrieval keeps user experience snappy without burning GPU cycles on massive prompts

card.h3: Simplicity and deep reasoning matter more than cost
ul: Your use case involves a single long document (e.g., 500-page contract, entire codebase) where retrieval fragmentation would lose context
Accuracy on multi-hop reasoning across a single source: long context models achieve 15–20% better F1 on narrative QA benchmarks vs RAG pipelines
You can tolerate higher per-query cost and slower response times for guaranteed coherence and no retrieval errors
The knowledge base changes rarely—long context avoids the overhead of chunking, indexing, and maintaining a vector store
